hero.tagline: Pioneering Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence, Graph Neural Networks, and Distributed Machine Learning for Real-World Impact.
hero.bioBrief: I conduct cutting-edge research at the intersection of Explainable AI (XAI), Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning, and Multimodal Deep Learning to build reliable and equitable intelligent systems.

biography: Semachew Molla Kassa is an Assistant Professor and Director of the Trustworthy AI Research Lab in the Department of Computer Science. His foundational research focuses on developing transparent, privacy-preserving, and computationally efficient machine learning models capable of operating robustly in complex, high-stakes environments.

His recent inquiries focus on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for biomedical network analysis, federated multi-agent learning architectures, and explainable deep learning representations for natural language processing.

Prior to his current academic appointment, Dr. Kassa served as a Senior Research Scientist at leading AI research labs and earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science with a specialization in Machine Learning and Data Science. He actively serves as an Associate Editor and PC Member for top-tier international conferences including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, and IEEE TPAMI.

description: Leading a team of 6 PhD students and postdoctoral fellows in trustworthy machine learning research.
Secured $1.2M+ in competitive research grants from national science foundations and industrial partners.
Teaching graduate-level courses: Advanced Deep Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Distributed AI.
Designed privacy-utility Pareto optimal algorithms for cross-silo federated learning in healthcare networks.
Co-authored 6 papers accepted in NeurIPS, ICML, and IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks.
Developed explainability pipelines (XAI) for multi-modal clinical diagnostic models.
Published open-source benchmarking toolkits utilized by over 40 research organizations worldwide.

areas.title: Explainable & Trustworthy AI
areas.summary: Developing mathematically grounded explanation mechanisms for complex deep neural networks.
areas.description: Our lab investigates how neural representations can be decoded into human-comprehensible concepts. We focus on counterfactual explanations, feature attribution stability, and causal discovery algorithms for high-stakes decision domains.

areas.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning
areas.summary: Architecting distributed machine learning systems that preserve data privacy without sacrificing model performance.
areas.description: We address non-IID data heterogeneity, communication bottlenecks, and differential privacy guarantees in multi-institutional federated learning setups across healthcare and IoT systems.

areas.title: Deep Graph Learning & Geometric Deep Learning
areas.summary: Building scalable neural networks designed for non-Euclidean graph structures and dynamic networks.
areas.description: Focusing on spatio-temporal graph convolutions, heterogeneous graph transformers, and topological neural networks applied to bio-molecular structures and knowledge graphs.

areas.title: Multimodal Retrieval & Reasoning
areas.summary: Cross-modal alignment between vision, structured graphs, and natural language representations.
areas.description: Exploring retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), and unified multimodal models tailored for low-resource languages and scientific literature synthesis.

projects.title: FedTrust: Robust & Private Federated Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: Designing differential privacy frameworks for heterogeneous graph representations in multi-site clinical diagnostic networks.
outcomes: Published 2 IEEE TPAMI papers on non-IID graph aggregation.
Released open-source FedTrust Python library with 800+ GitHub stars.

projects.title: X-NeuroGraph: Interpretability Pipelines for Brain Connectivity Networks
projects.summary: Extracting inspectable network motifs and subgraphs from functional MRI graph neural network classifiers.
outcomes: Identified novel neurological markers for early disease detection.
Demonstrated 94.2% diagnostic fidelity with human-in-the-loop validation.

projects.title: EthioNLP-Multimodal: Low-Resource Language Benchmarks
projects.summary: Building standardized datasets, tokenizers, and benchmark suites for Horn of Africa languages.
outcomes: Curated 5 core dataset benchmarks published at ACL 2023.
Adopted by international NLP research groups worldwide.

publications.title: Provably Fair and Private Federated Graph Learning via Optimal Transport
publications.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
publications.abstract: We present a unified optimal transport formulation for federated graph learning under heterogeneous domain shifts. Our method proves strict local privacy guarantees while bounding empirical accuracy degradation to under 1.8% compared to centralized training.

publications.title: Counterfactual Subgraph Explanations for Deep Graph Neural Networks
publications.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
publications.abstract: Graph neural network explanations frequently generate disconnected or unfeasible subgraphs. We propose SubgraphX-CF, a discrete optimization algorithm that guarantees connected, causal counterfactual explanations for molecular and social graphs.

publications.title: Differential Privacy Bottlenecks in Multi-Agent Autonomous Systems
publications.abstract: In multi-agent reinforcement learning, differential privacy noise quickly destabilizes cooperative policy convergence. We establish dynamic noise decay bounds that preserve convergence speed.

publications.title: Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence: Principles, Architectures, and Applications
publications.abstract: A comprehensive textbook detailing foundational algorithms for interpretable machine learning, robust defense against adversarial attacks, and ethical AI deployment frameworks.

publications.title: Multimodal Cross-Attention Alignment for Low-Resource Languages
publications.abstract: Cross-lingual transfer learning often degrades on morphologically rich low-resource languages. We introduce cross-attention adapter modules that leverage audio-text co-embedding.

publications.title: Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Epidemic Spread Dynamics
publications.venue: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD 2022)
publications.abstract: Predicting regional epidemic transmission requires modeling human mobility graphs alongside temporal infection counts. We propose ST-GNN with dynamic attention weights.
